conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been having pain in my left leg where I cut it on a shopping cart about three weeks ago. The wound hasn’t healed, and it’s been red and sore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And I understand you’ve also been having some diarrhea and stomach cramps?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. I was on doxycycline for the leg, but it made my stomach worse. I stopped it two days ago, and the diarrhea has gotten better since then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Sometimes antibiotics can upset the gut. We’ll hold off on antibiotics for now since your diarrhea is improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s good. I was worried it might be something serious like C. diff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We considered that, but since your symptoms are improving and you’re not having fevers, we don’t think it’s active now. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’ve reviewed your history. You’ve been through a lot—stem cell transplant, GVHD, blood clots, and diabetes. We’ll make sure everything is managed carefully.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been a long road. I’m on so many medications, I sometimes lose track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go over them together. For now, we started you on vancomycin just in case the leg wound was infected, but we’re watching closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is the wound infected? It still hurts.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s red and tender, but the blood work doesn’t show a big infection, and the wound culture came back with no growth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No bacteria at all?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That suggests it’s not a typical infection. Sometimes wounds don’t heal because of dead tissue blocking the process.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what happens now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve consulted surgery. They’ll do a bedside debridement tomorrow to remove the dead tissue and help the wound heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you pain medication beforehand. It’s usually well tolerated. After that, wound care will teach the nurses how to dress it properly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds okay. I just want it to heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We do too. Also, your IgG level was low, which isn’t surprising with your history of GVHD. We’re giving you IV immunoglobulin today to help boost your immunity.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had that before. It helps with infections, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it gives your body extra antibodies. We’ll continue your usual medications for GVHD, diabetes, and blood thinners as well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m on Lovenox twice a day for my clots. Please don’t stop that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We won’t. You’ll continue that exactly as prescribed. We’ve also checked an X-ray of your leg—no foreign body or bone infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried something was stuck in there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Morning, Doctor. My stomach feels much better. No diarrhea since yesterday morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re stopping the vancomycin because the wound doesn’t appear infected. The plan is still to debride it this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no more antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. Since there’s no infection, we don’t want to overuse antibiotics, especially given your history of gut issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I’ve had this problem before with antibiotics causing diarrhea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll manage your pain with Dilaudid as needed. The wound care team will see you after the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, just checking in after your debridement. How’s the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s sore, but the medicine helps. They cleaned out a lot of tissue, didn’t they?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they removed non-viable tissue that was preventing healing. The wound looks much cleaner now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hope it starts healing now. I’ve lost about 5 pounds in the last two weeks because I wasn’t eating well with the stomach issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s significant. But you said your appetite is coming back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’m starting to feel hungry again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good news. We’ll monitor your weight, but it sounds like the diarrhea was the main cause.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are stable, and you’re doing well. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue your regular medications. For the wound, keep it clean and dressed as the nurses showed you. Watch for redness, swelling, or pus.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if it starts draining?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor or go to urgent care. You have a follow-up with wound clinic next week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the Dilaudid?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving you 20 tablets for breakthrough pain. Take it only if needed, every 6 hours as needed. You shouldn’t need it long-term.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my diarrhea—if it comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re adding loperamide to your list—take it only if diarrhea returns. But avoid antibiotics unless absolutely necessary.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and keep up with your follow-ups. We’ll see you in clinic if needed.
